bridge: Builds on C04 object lifetime, L02 permissions and C05 execution. Observe only your own processes and files.
teaching:
An operating system multiplexes hardware and mediates access. A process has an execution context and an address-space view; a thread is an execution path within a process. Virtual memory maps process-visible addresses to underlying storage, so equal-looking virtual addresses in two processes need not refer to the same physical memory.

User mode limits what ordinary instructions may do. A system call enters the kernel to request services such as opening a file. The kernel checks relevant credentials and object permissions. A library function can wrap a system call, but not every function call enters the kernel. Page protection also distinguishes readable, writable and executable mappings.

A filesystem maps names to objects and metadata. A file descriptor refers to an open-file interface, not merely a filename string. Renaming or unlinking a path does not necessarily terminate an already-open descriptor. Trace identity, name resolution, permission checks and object lifetime separately when explaining access.

Keep account privilege separate from CPU mode: an administrator’s program normally executes in user mode and enters kernel mode through controlled mechanisms. The trusted computing base consists of components relied upon to enforce the policy; a failure inside it can undermine that policy. Reducing it is useful, but size alone does not prove correctness. The video’s 4 KiB mapping is one hardware example. File descriptors refer to opened objects, whereas pathnames require lookup. Journaling records selected filesystem updates for crash recovery; it does not promise every application write is atomic, durable or backed up. An application may need a documented write/flush/rename protocol under the specific filesystem contract.
example:
Own process A          Own process B
virtual address 0x1000  virtual address 0x1000
      |                       |
 mapping A                mapping B
      v                       v
 physical page X          physical page Y

Read path:
program -> open(path) -> kernel permission check -> descriptor
program -> read(descriptor) -> bytes or error
explanation: The diagram explains isolation, not a promise that these exact addresses exist. A shared-memory mapping can deliberately make two processes access the same underlying page. File mode checks depend on the process identity and path traversal, so a filename alone is not enough to determine the result.
exercise: Create a harmless private file inside a practice directory. Record its owner and mode, the directory mode, and the process identity used to read it. Draw the request path through the kernel and state which observations are evidence versus assumptions.
solution: A sound record includes both directory traversal and file permissions, the current unprivileged identity and successful read-back. It does not claim that an administrator is prevented from accessing the file.
challenge: Two processes each print an identical virtual pointer value. Is that sufficient to prove shared memory? Explain what mapping evidence would be required. Separately explain why a library call and a system call are different concepts.
challenge_solution: Identical virtual values do not prove shared backing. You need explicit shared mappings or equivalent OS evidence. A library routine executes user-space code and may invoke zero, one or several system calls.
